title: Feed Me Weird Things
desc_lfm_album: Feed Me Weird Things is the debut studio album by Squarepusher. It was released on Rephlex Records in 1996. A remastered 25th anniversary edition was released in 2021 on Warp Records -Released: 3 June 1996 (Remaster: 3 June 2021) -Genre: Drill 'n' Bass, Intelligent Dance Music, Jungle, Jazz Fusion -Length: 66:43 (Remaster: 76:17) -Label: Rephlex (Remaster: Warp) -Producer: Tom Jenkinson .
desc_lfm_artist: Squarepusher is a pseudonym of Chelmsford, Essex, England, electronic musician Tom Jenkinson (b. 1975), best known for his experimental drum and bass, with a heavy jazz fusion influence.  A skilled bassist and multi-instrumentalist, Jenkinson's virtuoso playing is a staple of his music and one of the more obvious affiliations with jazz (although his formal arrangements are often as jazz-derived as his playing). His bass style includes melodic fretless playing, high-speed slap bass and intricate chordal work.

title: We Had Good Times Together, Don't Forget That
desc_lfm_album: we had good times together, don't forget that is the final album released under the Sewerslvt alias. It was written primarily as a tribute to Jvne's late girlfriend Angel, who overdosed while in the care of medical professionals. Jvne had intended to either end the Sewerslvt project or take an extended hiatus after the release of Skitzofrenia Simulation in June 2021, but after news broke of the events in their personal life, they decided to create the final Sewerslvt album. The Sewerslvt brand and reputation had taken a toll on Jvne, and with the loss of their girlfriend as well, .
desc_lfm_artist: Sewerslvt (formerly Jvnko and Sadboy Sheldon) is a drum and bass / breakcore / electonic artist from Sydney, Australia.

title: If You're Into It, I'm Out of It
desc_lfm_album: If You're Into It, I'm Out of It is the second album by electronic producer Christoph de Babalon, initially released on September 15, 1997 through Digital Hardcore Recordings. It is noted for its dark, heavy atmosphere, as it combines the musical stylings of dark ambient, breakcore, and drum and bass. Since its release, it has gained a cult following and received much critical praise. .
desc_lfm_artist: Christoph de Babalon is known for tripping beats, dark wide spaces and eternal melancholy. He released his first record in 1994 on Hamburg's cult-label Fischkopf. This record (as well as all that followed over the next years) were extensively played by BBC-DJ-legend John Peel. Right after his debut he began working with Alec Empire's Digital Hardcore Recordings (DHR) where he, besides a couple of other records released his most important work: the legendary album 'If You're Into It, I'm Out of It'.

title: Timeless
desc_lfm_album: Timeless is the debut studio album by British electronic musician Goldie. It was released on 7 August 1995 and is universally regarded as a groundbreaking release in the history of drum and bass music. Goldie was joined in the studio by engineer/producer Rob Playford (founder of the Moving Shadow label), who did most of the programming and production, with Goldie generating the musical ideas, rhythms and arrangements. Additional engineering and production came from Dego and Marc Mac of 4hero. Diane Charlemagne contributed the bulk of the vocals. Its title track includes what has become the most recognisable and crossover hit .

desc_lfm_artist:
4hero are a UK act based in Dollis Hill, North-West London. The main members of this group are Dennis 'Dego' McFarlane and Mark 'Marc Mac' Clair. As well as being a recording artists, they also run the Reinforced record label.

They are renowned as pioneers and frontrunners in jungle and drum and bass, and the group obtained a Mercury Music Prize nomination for their 1998 album Two Pages. Their style was initially uptempo breakbeat house and techno, and has progressed to hardcore, jungle, and drum 'n' bass.

desc_lfm_artist:
DJ Spooky, That Subliminal Kid (born Paul Miller, 1970), is a Washington DC-born illbient and trip-hop musician, turntablist and producer. He borrowed his stage name from a character in a William S. Burroughs novel.

Growing up in DC, Spooky became interested in punk and go-go music, and attended Bowdoin College in Maine, earning degrees in French literature and philosophy. He began writing science fiction and formed a collective called Soundlab with several other artists.
